text: Tipped in! Anunoby tips it in!
Game 4 of the Finals. The Spurs led by as many as 29 at Madison Square Garden, and lost by one.

text: In all the years of the Finals, no team had ever blown a lead that big. The Spurs now own that record.
Afterward, everyone said bad shots, mental collapse. Not wrong. But I went through the tracking data, and it's not that simple.
Start with the first half. Just how hot were the Spurs?
41 to 22 after one. 14 threes in the half, the most in Finals history. Everything was falling.
say: Forty-one to twenty-two after one. Fourteen threes in the half, the most in Finals history. Everything was falling.

text: But look closely, and a lot of these shots weren't easy.

text: That extra 21 points was a hot hand. And a hot hand comes and goes. You can't ride it for a whole game.
say: That extra twenty-one points was a hot hand. And a hot hand comes and goes. You can't ride it for a whole game.

text: So where did the lead start to slip?

text: And here's the thing: he already had 3 flagrant points this postseason. One more, and he's suspended. In the Finals. So how freely can he play now?

text: From those two free throws, the Knicks ripped off a 13-0 run.

text: Barkley wasn't wrong. With a lead that big, why keep jacking threes? Where's the logic in that?
So in the fourth, skip the threes and attack the rim. The Spurs did exactly that. The result? 4 for 19.

text: Why? Because the Knicks were right in their faces. On Spurs shots, the nearest defender's hand averaged just 2.7 feet from the ball. Less than an arm's length. How do you shoot over that?

Pinned on the glass!

That one play handed the Knicks a free possession. A whole night's work, gone.
